test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What happens if the accused minister (Prime Minister / Chief Minister) is granted bail within 30 days according to the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025?

options.text: They are automatically disqualified for 5 years.
They are removed from office permanently.
No action is taken; they can continue in office.
They are suspended from their post for 30 more days.

solution:
The correct answer is __**No action is taken; they can continue in office**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025**, introduces specific provisions regarding the administrative continuity of the **Prime Minister** and **Chief Ministers** in the event of their arrest or legal detention.
 
• According to the bill, if an accused minister, such as the **Prime Minister** or a **Chief Minister**, is granted **bail** within a window of **30 days** from the date of arrest, **no action is taken** against their position.
 
• This ensures that the individual can **continue in office** and perform their constitutional duties without being subjected to automatic **suspension** or **disqualification**, provided the legal stay is brief.
 
• The bill aims to balance the legal rights of the **accused** with the necessity of maintaining stability in the executive branch of the **government**.
 
• If the individual fails to secure **bail** within the stipulated **30-day** period, the bill prescribes further consequences, but the immediate **30-day** period serves as a protective grace window.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 368:** The **Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025**, would be processed under **Article 368** of the **Constitution of India**, which grants **Parliament** the power to amend the document through a **Special Majority**.
 
• **Representation of the People Act, 1951:** Historically, **Section 8** of this **Act** deals with the **disqualification** of representatives upon **conviction**. However, the new **2025 amendment** specifically addresses the status of ministers at the **accused** stage before a final verdict is reached.
 
• **Governance Continuity:** The bill addresses the recent legal and political debates in **India** (observed in cases during **2023** and **2024**) concerning whether a **Chief Minister** can run the **government** from judicial custody.
 
• **Judicial Custody vs. Police Custody:** The **30-day** limit applies regardless of whether the official is in **police custody** or **judicial custody**, emphasizing the availability of **bail** as the determining factor for continuing in office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **30-Day Threshold:** The **numerical value** of **30 days** is critical; it serves as a legislative compromise to prevent the **misuse** of investigative agencies to topple **governments** through short-term arrests.
 
• **Executive Stability:** The provision that **no action is taken** reflects the principle that the mandate of the **electorate** should not be subverted by mere allegations unless the detention is prolonged enough to hinder **governance**.
 
• **Role of the President and Governor:** Under this bill, the **President** (for the **PM**) and the **Governor** (for the **CM**) are required to wait for the expiration of the **30-day** period before initiating any constitutional process for **suspension** or replacement.
 
• **Legal Precedents:** This amendment seeks to codify matters that were previously left to judicial interpretation by the **Supreme Court** or the **High Courts** regarding the "morality" of holding office while under **arrest**.
</ul
